Returns verified child paths/digests, derivations, uncovered ranges, unknown chunks and extraction_gaps with continuation_id recovery instructions. Linux, format-specific extractors, prlimit and procps ps are required. Preserves the sandbox and publishes only regular files; no mounts or extracted-code execution. Select a returned native file with open_binary for analysis. Decompressed offsets are not original-file addresses.

reaTools.name: inspect_uefi_firmware
reaTools.description: Map PI firmware volumes, FFS files, section chains, AMD PSP directory candidates and uncovered ranges in a local flash image. Report integrity observations and coverage limits. LZMA-custom, LZMAF86, and AMD-zlib streams can contain nested volumes or section chains. Decoded offsets are relative to the stream identified by source_stream. EFI standard compression and other unsupported handlers remain explicit limitations.

reaTools.name: extract_uefi_firmware
reaTools.description: Extract FFS bodies and section payloads from a local UEFI image into an absent directory. A volume, file or section selection includes its descendants. Use source_stream with an offset from a decoded stream or when offsets are ambiguous. Results include SHA-256, source ranges and decode derivations; original_file_range is null for decoded bytes. Unsupported carriers are optional and decoding gaps remain visible. Pass an extracted PE32 file to open_binary for executable analysis.

reaTools.name: inspect_uefi_nvram
reaTools.description: Map valid AMI NVAR entries inside a local flash image, including nested factory defaults such as StdDefaults. Reports raw link displacements, attributes, inline GUIDs or GUID-table indices, data ranges and SHA-256 digests. Data-only records have no name or GUID reference. Links describe the image bytes. The parser walks physical records and reports the nesting depth and parent offset. No external tools or target execution are required.

reaTools.name: inspect_android_jni_bindings
reaTools.description: Link an APK's DEX native declarations to Java_* exports and static JNINativeMethod candidates by ABI and exact library occurrence, without executing it or loading libraries. Returns digests, relation IDs, slot/relocation provenance and explicit partial/unknown coverage; a candidate match does not prove uniqueness or runtime registration. Declaration filters and ABI/library filters narrow results; RegisterNatives attribution uses the full declaration inventory first. Default summary retains complete Evidence. Optional view kind android-jni selects bindings/declarations/candidates/libraries, fields and pages; use inspect_analysis_view with parent_evidence_id for later pages. Empty selections match none. Requires caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK.

reaTools.name: inspect_android_package
reaTools.description: Inspect APK package/SDK/permission declarations, decoded manifest, static components and class/resource counts without executing it or verifying signatures. Requires caller-supplied JADX MCP JAR and JDK. Default complete returns full Evidence; detail summary retains it and omits manifest text/raw duplicates. With summary, view kind android selects facet components (exact filters, fields, paging), component-summary or manifest (UTF-16 text pages); complete detail rejects view. Use normalized_result.parent_evidence_id with inspect_analysis_view for later views. Component source_index identifies the original declaration, and declaration_coverage marks partial declarations.

reaTools.name: search_android_classes
reaTools.description: Search complete top-level decompiler class-name rows in an explicit local APK by case-sensitive substring. Empty query inventories all rows. Repeated names remain repeated and appear in duplicate_names; the provider accepts only class names for lookup, so these rows do not identify which same-name class node a later lookup selects. Retains artifact and engine identity; no APK execution.

reaTools.name: inspect_android_class
reaTools.description: Inspect one exact Android class's methods, fields, inner classes, DEX prototypes and encoded static final values without generating source. Select an overload_index from these results for inspect_android_method; indices are artifact/engine-session scoped and prototypes are not complete raw method IDs. Optional mapping_path adds verified R8/ProGuard names separately; observed names remain primary. detail summary retains complete Evidence and returns normalized symbols without duplicate raw calls; complete remains the default.

reaTools.name: inspect_android_method
reaTools.description: Decompile one Android method, with explicit overload_index when names collide and smali fallback when needed. Reports DEX prototype, representation, fallback markers and source truncation; display signatures may be aliases. Optional mapping_path annotates R8/ProGuard names without replacing observed names. detail summary retains complete Evidence and returns the selected body without duplicate class metadata; complete remains the default. Use inspect_android_class to choose the overload.

reaTools.name: trace_android_references
reaTools.description: Trace incoming static using nodes to an exact Android class or selected method overload. A method target may be an external class directly named by DEX invokes: target_definition external and reference_scope direct_dex_invokes identify this narrower inventory, without inventing a class definition or body. Ambiguous external requests list observed DEX prototypes; select overload_index explicitly. For APK-defined targets use inspect_android_class. The total counts containing nodes, not individual invokes. External callers include source_selector for inspect_android_method. Source lines and the containing node dex_offset remain unknown. direct_invokes carries exact DEX code-unit offsets when available; direct_invokes_exhaustive false marks byte-bounded partial instruction evidence, and null means unknown. No reflection, JNI or runtime dispatch is inferred.

reaTools.name: inspect_pcap_client
reaTools.description: Inspect the caller-selected tshark and capinfos binaries: selected commands, selection sources, and versions. Both tools must be usable. Reads no capture file. REA never installs the Wireshark suite; select binaries with REA_TSHARK_COMMAND and REA_CAPINFOS_COMMAND (absolute) or from PATH.

reaTools.name: inspect_pcap_capture
reaTools.description: Summarize a saved pcap/pcapng snapshot: exact packet count, SHA-256, IP endpoints, DNS questions/addresses, TLS SNI, protocols and HTTP URIs. Use inspect_packet_capture for caller-selected TShark fields or display filters. Default complete returns full Evidence; detail summary retains it for inspect_analysis_view kind pcap. Unknown DNS attribution and excluded credentials stay explicit. Requires caller-supplied capinfos/tshark and Linux prlimit or Windows Job Objects; never captures live traffic.

reaTools.name: identify_flutter_build
reaTools.description: Identify a Flutter app's build facts by pure parsing: observed Dart snapshot hashes from lib/<abi>/libapp.so, per-ABI library digests, the engine library's GNU build-id, and any labeled Dart version or toolchain strings libflutter.so carries. Complete snapshot coverage currently expects two independent headers in the legacy split VM/isolate profile; unified and other layouts can yield partial build facts. The snapshot hash maps to a Dart SDK release through an external dataset; REA performs no lookup. No engine, no execution, no external tools.

reaTools.name: inspect_dart_aot
reaTools.description: Inspect one APK ABI's Dart AOT snapshot without executing it. Supports legacy split VM/isolate FullAOT kind 3 and unified FullAOT kind 2. Returns the observed profile, snapshot exports, headers, hashes and bounded package:/dart:/identifier-like byte-pattern strings. pool_policy.contains selects strings before collection; other pool budgets do not raise APK/ELF/response limits. Default complete returns all facts; detail summary retains them for inspect_analysis_view kind dart-aot, collections package_uris/dart_uris/class_like_tokens, using parent_evidence_id and row paging. Counts are lower bounds and page exhaustion never proves complete pool coverage.

reaTools.name: list_frida_devices
reaTools.description: List Frida devices currently available to this host, optionally connecting to the caller-selected remote Frida endpoint. Remote authentication options are used for this call only and are never returned or recorded.

reaTools.name: list_frida_processes
reaTools.description:
List processes observed on a selected Frida device or caller-supplied remote endpoint. A remote connection is closed after discovery; authentication values are never returned or recorded.

Provide exactly one of device_id or remote. device_id selects a device (use "local" for this host); remote requires an address.

reaTools.name: start_frida_session
reaTools.description: Attach Frida to one selected process or spawn one selected target. Spawned targets remain paused until resume_frida_session, allowing scripts to load before execution. Closing a session detaches instrumentation; it does not kill the target.

reaTools.name: load_frida_script
reaTools.description: Load caller-supplied JavaScript into a Frida session. Scripts can read or change target memory and behavior and can access the target process's capabilities. Messages and script errors are returned inline as Evidence; source content is not persisted.

reaTools.name: resume_frida_session
reaTools.description: Resume the process created by a paused Frida spawn session. Attached processes are already running and cannot be resumed through this operation.

reaTools.name: unload_frida_script
reaTools.description: Unload one caller-selected Frida script from a live session. This removes that script's instrumentation from the target.

reaTools.name: frida_session_status
reaTools.description: Read observed Frida session state on each call. Default detail=complete returns queued script messages and capture truncation. detail=summary retains the complete observation in this session and returns identity, state, scripts, retained message count and truncation without payloads. Export the complete parent with export_evidence_bundle; retained summaries are historical and never refresh live state.

reaTools.name: close_frida_session
reaTools.description: Unload session scripts and attempt to detach REA's Frida session. Then resume a still-paused spawned process if script cleanup or session detach confirms instrumentation was released. Cleanup failures are reported. REA never kills the target; its final state is reported as unknown.

reaTools.name: instrument_with_frida
reaTools.description: Run caller-authored Frida JavaScript against a selected process for one observation window, then detach. Scripts can read/change target memory and behavior and use the process's capabilities. CLI and MCP share this ephemeral workflow; use start_frida_session/load_frida_script for a persistent session. Remote authentication is call-local and excluded from Evidence. Detachment does not establish target termination.

reaTools.name: inspect_apktool_client
reaTools.description: Inspect the caller-selected apktool launcher: resolved command, selection source, and version. Decodes nothing. REA never installs Apktool or Java; select a launcher with REA_APKTOOL_COMMAND (absolute) or apktool on PATH.

reaTools.name: decode_android_resources
reaTools.description: Decode APK resources with apktool d --no-src: readable manifest, version/SDK facts, string resources/locales and decoded file count. Uses a temporary workspace removed after projection; smali/source recovery belongs to JADX. Strings default to 2000 valid entries per table; use string_offset/string_limit and table.page.next_offset for later pages, checking target.sha256 across calls. Per-call string budgets can be raised without restart. decode_timeout_ms controls decoding (default 600000 ms), independently of output capture and version probes.

reaTools.name: inspect_jeb_client
reaTools.description: Inspect the running JEB client serving MCP: engine version, GUI or headless mode, and startup time. Does not open a target. Requires a caller-started JEB client reachable at REA_JEB_MCP_URL (default http://127.0.0.1:8425/mcp); REA never installs or launches JEB.

reaTools.name: open_jeb_project
reaTools.description: Open or create a JEB project from an artifact file or existing .jdb2 database on the engine host. Returns the project's input-file digests and top-level units. The engine analyzes the target itself; REA does not read the file or execute it. Fails when a project is already open.

reaTools.name: list_jeb_units
reaTools.description: List project units by stable unit path and type, with optional wildcard filter, parent restriction, and pagination. The engine caps pages at 100 units; a full page reports partial coverage because more units may exist. Read-only.

reaTools.name: decompile_jeb_item
reaTools.description: Decompile one type or method to engine pseudo-code using its decompiler (Dalvik, Java, or native). item_address comes from the engine's code item listing; unit_path defaults to the engine's first code unit and stays unknown when omitted. Read-only with respect to the target file.

reaTools.name: inspect_adb_client
reaTools.description: Inspect the caller-selected adb client: resolved binary, version, and install path. Never contacts devices and never starts the adb server. REA never installs platform tools; select a binary with REA_ADB_PATH (absolute) or adb on PATH.

reaTools.name: list_adb_devices
reaTools.description: List attached devices exactly as `adb devices -l` reports them: serial, state, transport, model metadata, and an inferred emulator/physical kind with its evidence basis. Emulators and USB or network devices appear alike; REA neither starts nor manages them. transport_id_text preserves exact full-range transport identity; transport_id is its safe numeric projection or null. May start the local adb server on first use.

reaTools.name: inspect_adb_device
reaTools.description: Inspect one device's build identity through a fixed `getprop` whitelist: Android and SDK versions, security patch, fingerprint, product identity, CPU ABIs, and debuggable flag, plus the observed emulator indicator ro.kernel.qemu. Present properties retain empty values; omitted keys were not reported. Read-only with respect to the device.

reaTools.name: list_adb_packages
reaTools.description: List installed packages on one device with each base APK's device path, optionally scoped to third-party or system packages. Paths are device filesystem paths, not host-local. Read-only.

reaTools.name: pull_adb_package
reaTools.description: Pull one installed package's complete APK set (base plus every split, as `pm path` reports) from the device into a caller-selected output directory, creating a package-named subdirectory that must not already exist. Every pulled file is digested with SHA-256; partial pulls keep successful artifacts and per-file failure reasons. The device keeps the originals.

reaTools.name: read_adb_logcat
reaTools.description: Read a bounded dump of the device log (`logcat -d -t`) for one buffer, optionally restricted to a process id. No streaming, no clearing; the newest lines are kept when the count cap trims. Read-only.

reaTools.name: inspect_adb_package
reaTools.description: Inspect installed-package versions, install times, installer, user id, flags, and requested-permission count through read-only `dumpsys package`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in bounded numeric_issues and make coverage partial; version_code stays exact text. Unknown sections are not inferred.

reaTools.name: pull_adb_file
reaTools.description: Pull one absolute device path (a database, shared-preferences XML, or any readable file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it with SHA-256. The local copy must not already exist. Read-only with respect to the device.

reaTools.name: push_adb_file
reaTools.description: Push one local file to an absolute device path. If the destination is an existing directory, adb places the file inside it under the local basename and the result reports that file path. A device-mutating tool: checks for an existing destination file before transfer and refuses it unless overwrite is explicitly requested; this check is not atomic and another process can create the path before adb writes. The private staged copy remains non-writable and preserves source executable bits. When the device provides sha256sum, the transfer is verified by comparing it with the local digest.

reaTools.name: capture_adb_screen
reaTools.description: Capture one frame of the device screen as a PNG (`screencap -p` through exec-out, no device-side file) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting it and reporting its dimensions. No recording or interaction.

reaTools.name: list_adb_processes
reaTools.description: List running processes exactly as `ps -A` reports them: user, pid, ppid, rss, state, and name. Useful for pairing with instrumentation lanes. Read-only.

reaTools.name: list_adb_directory
reaTools.description: List the immediate children of one absolute device directory, including hidden entries: names, kinds, permissions, owner, group, sizes, dates, and symlink targets. Names and targets preserve embedded newlines. Recognizes the standard errors for absent paths and denied reads. Read-only.

reaTools.name: list_adb_features
reaTools.description: List the device's declared hardware and software features (`pm list features`) for device fingerprinting. Read-only.

reaTools.name: list_adb_services
reaTools.description: List the device's binder services with their interfaces (`service list`). Read-only.

reaTools.name: inspect_adb_display
reaTools.description: Read physical and override size/density from `wm size` and `wm density`. Malformed numeric declarations are retained in numeric_issues with partial coverage; optional values remain null. Required physical-size failures retain partial display facts. Read-only.

reaTools.name: inspect_adb_window
reaTools.description: Report the window manager's focus declarations with display context, original lines and explicit summary status. Reads `dumpsys window windows`, falling back to `displays` only when no focus field is declared. Singular fields are unknown for multiple contexts or repeated declarations; inspect focus_contexts for every observation. Read-only; no interaction occurs.

reaTools.name: read_adb_setting
reaTools.description: Read one settings value (`settings get`) from the system, secure, or global namespace. Absent keys report the device's own null observation. Read-only; writing settings is not exposed.

reaTools.name: collect_adb_bugreport
reaTools.description: Collect one device-generated bugreport archive (`adb bugreport`) into a caller-selected output directory, digesting the zip. The archive contains the device's own dumpstate, dumpsys, and logcat report; collection can take minutes. Read-only with respect to configuration.

reaTools.name: resolve_adb_packages
reaTools.description: Find installed packages by case-insensitive package-name substring and return each base APK device path. Pass an exact returned name to pull_adb_package to retrieve its base and split APKs. Read-only.

reaTools.name: install_adb_package
reaTools.description: Install one local APK on the device (`adb install [-r]`), recording the APK's host digest and byte size. A device-mutating tool: `replace_requested` records whether `-r` was selected; `replaced` is null because install success does not establish prior package state. The device's own Success/Failure verdict is preserved with its reason.

reaTools.name: uninstall_adb_package
reaTools.description: Request package removal for user 0 (`adb shell pm uninstall --user 0`) without data retention. A device-mutating tool; absent packages report the device's own refusal reason.

reaTools.name: start_adb_app
reaTools.description: Start one installed app's resolved launcher activity with `am start -W -n`. A device-mutating tool for dynamic analysis. The full wait report determines success; failures retain launch-attempt facts and raw output. Pair with `read_adb_logcat` (pid filter) and `list_adb_processes` to observe the app, and `stop_adb_app` to end the run.

reaTools.name: start_adb_activity
reaTools.description: Start an intent with `am start -W`: one action, optional data URI, optional explicit component, and up to 16 typed extras (string, boolean, int, long, float). A device-mutating tool; the full wait report determines success, with failed-attempt facts and raw output retained.

reaTools.name: stop_adb_app
reaTools.description: Force-stop every process of one package (`am force-stop`), ending a dynamic-analysis run. A device-mutating tool; it succeeds whether or not the package had running processes.

reaTools.name: list_browser_targets
reaTools.description: List pages exposed by one loopback Chrome DevTools Protocol endpoint, optionally filtered by exact origin. Returns target IDs and URLs; query values and fragments are preserved, with URL userinfo credentials removed. Use a returned target ID with inspect_web_page. discovery_timeout_ms controls discovery; command_timeout_ms does not apply. Browser-socket endpoints remain shared by the active browser provider until it closes or target-session cleanup is unconfirmed; cancellation/deadline on a clean socket releases only this call’s lease.

reaTools.name: inspect_web_page
reaTools.description:
Passively inspect one selected page target through CDP without evaluating JavaScript, navigating, clicking, closing, or mutating the page. If no origin filter is supplied, capture is scoped to the target's current origin. Returns DOM structure, accessibility, scripts, resources, attach-window network and console metadata, workers, and redacted storage inventory as Evidence.

Provide a complete input group: cdp_endpoint + target_id + [allowed_origins] + [discovery_timeout_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [observation_ms] + [include_accessibility_text] + [include_console_text] + [include_json_body_shapes] + [include_websocket_shapes] + [include_storage_keys] + [include_storage_fingerprints] + [include_script_sources]; cdp_endpoint + target_id + include_script_sources + [allowed_origins] + [discovery_timeout_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [observation_ms] + [include_accessibility_text] + [include_console_text] + [include_json_body_shapes] + [include_websocket_shapes] + [include_storage_keys] + [include_storage_fingerprints].

reaTools.name: analyze_web_bundle
reaTools.description:
Recover a static chunk graph, route/endpoint candidates, vendor fingerprints and page-declared WebMCP metadata from JavaScript on one selected CDP page. May fetch source maps only from the target origin or explicitly selected origins; application JavaScript is not executed. detail summary retains complete Evidence; view {kind: "web-bundle", collection: "endpoints"} selects endpoint rows, and javascript-routes views select route patterns/occurrences/sources/unknowns. Read later pages with inspect_analysis_view. Static candidates do not establish runtime reachability or a complete route set.

Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.

reaTools.name: observe_web_session
reaTools.description: Arm a CDP observation window of the requested duration while the user operates the page. By default it follows the selected target's current origin; an explicit origin list controls which origins may be retained. Records navigation, redirect, lifecycle, and failure events.

reaTools.name: discover_webmcp_tools
reaTools.description: Passively inventory every page-registered WebMCP tool and its complete structural input-schema summary using the experimental CDP WebMCP domain. Metadata is page-declared-untrusted; REA never registers or invokes discovered tools.

reaTools.name: compare_web_captures
reaTools.description:
Compare two passive page inspections or two recorded browser scenarios. For passive captures, pass before/after with each complete inspect_web_page normalized_result in inspection and optional complete discover_webmcp_tools normalized_result in webmcp. For scenarios, pass complete normalized_result objects as before_scenario/after_scenario; use exactly one input group. Returns artifact differences and alignment failures. Scenario steps align by exact IDs; optional literal normalization is recorded. HTTP requests and ordered WebSocket streams are compared without inventing stable identities for same-URL connections. Missing or truncated Evidence never proves equality.

Provide a complete input group: before + after; before_scenario + after_scenario + [normalization].

reaTools.name: capture_web_screenshot
reaTools.description: Capture the current visible viewport of one configured page as an inline, content-addressed PNG artifact. The operation never scrolls, navigates, or evaluates page JavaScript.

reaTools.name: compare_web_screenshots
reaTools.description: Compare two self-verifying PNG screenshot artifacts with local pixel metrics. Returns exact changed-pixel ratios and channel deltas without OCR or external services.

reaTools.name: capture_browser_scenario
reaTools.description:
Drive a browser scenario when passive observation cannot exercise the app. Launch the selected executable or connect to a loopback CDP target; actions can change application state and make network requests. Supply browser, start_url and actions, e.g. {browser:{mode:"launch",executable_path:"/opt/chromium/chrome"},start_url:{url:"https://app.example.test/"},actions:[{step_id:"settle",action:"wait_for_timeout",duration_ms:250}]}. Empty storage and a URL-only final capture are defaults. Request actions use page fetch on the start origin; capture.network independently opts into request_body, response_body and header_values. Credentials and declared secrets are redacted. capture.limits controls retained event/content budgets; omissions identify affected events/transactions. Role locators match the exact full accessible name. Actions wait for completion or cancellation; per-action timeout_ms bounds a step. Default complete delivery returns Evidence inline. detail summary retains it and returns step outcomes, final/first-unsuccessful accessibility, and counts; inspect_analysis_view kind browser-scenario pages steps, events, transactions and UTF-16 text. Use inspect_web_page for observation without actions.

reaTools.name: observe_web_execution
reaTools.description: Instrument one selected CDP page for a finite, externally driven precise coverage window. Resets execution counters and prevents optimized execution until stopped. Returns complete nested UTF-16 ranges/counts, independently hashed script text and request initiator associations by session script ID. Does not navigate, click, evaluate selected code or close the externally owned page. Navigation ends document-scoped collection; workers and UI causality remain outside this claim. Emits an actual armed progress notification before external actions.

reaTools.name: inspect_web_event_listeners
reaTools.description: Inspect listeners registered directly on the first main-document CSS match in one selected CDP page. Returns event flags, native callback locations, source ownership and exact script text/digests inline. Does not dispatch events, evaluate JavaScript or invoke handlers. Delegated ancestor/framework listeners and execution history remain unknown. Releases REA's object group and transport, preserving the external page.

reaTools.name: inspect_web_network_capture
reaTools.description: Inspect a saved local HAR 1.2, mitmproxy, Fiddler SAZ or supported aioquic qlog capture without contacting recorded URLs. Returns source-linked records, preserved producer fields, precise numbers, exposed bytes and explicit coverage/limitations; transport credentials and explicitly marked sensitive values are excluded. Use inspect_web_page for a live CDP page. Preserve capture_path exactly as supplied; it names a path on the REA host, not a path to rebase onto the client workspace. Select format; record_ordinals selects records after full decoding and also decodes recognized protobuf/gRPC bodies. Optional protobuf selects body_pointers, framing and a local FileDescriptorSet/message_type; native gRPC and gRPC-web remain distinct, ambiguous readings stay candidates and compressed payloads stay unknown. Default complete delivery is inline. detail summary retains Evidence for inspect_analysis_view kind capture (preview/complete), protobuf (bodies/frames/fields), or qlog; large text/schema values require explicit fields. Qlog supports aioquic 1.5.0 JSON qlog 0.3 and reports STREAM interval unions/endpoint loss declarations, not recovered bodies or proved network loss. SAZ preserves encoded bytes without replay/HAR conversion; encrypted archives are unsupported. Mitmproxy requires caller-supplied mitmdump 12.2.3 on Linux. Malformed or oversized captures return no partial success; browser transaction attribution and HAR text’s original bytes remain unknown.

reaTools.name: list_electron_targets
reaTools.description: List every Electron file:// page target from a selected loopback CDP endpoint. Local file paths are canonicalized after symlink resolution. Selecting an endpoint exposes every eligible target and its local path metadata.

reaTools.name: inspect_electron_page
reaTools.description:
Passively inspect one Electron file page by supplying its loopback CDP endpoint and target ID. The provider rechecks that the target currently exists at that endpoint and is a local file page. Returns frames, DOM structure, resource paths, and scripts without evaluating renderer JavaScript or invoking Electron APIs. The selected endpoint exposes every local file page and its metadata to this tool.

Provide a complete input group: cdp_endpoint + target_id + [observation_ms] + [command_timeout_ms] + [include_script_sources]; cdp_endpoint + target_id + include_script_sources + [observation_ms] + [command_timeout_ms].

reaTools.name: analyze_javascript_application
reaTools.description:
Build a static application graph from a local ASAR or extracted JavaScript app without executing it. Supply input_path, e.g. {input_path:"/apps/client",source_paths:["main.js"],detail:"summary"}. Copy source_paths exactly from the inventory, not host-absolute paths inferred from input_path. Returns nodes, edges, semantic relations, integrity contradictions, coverage and unknowns. source_paths limits source analysis to exact inventoried paths without narrowing inventory or artifact identity; dependencies are not implicitly analyzed and unselected sources remain unknown. detail summary reduces delivery, retaining complete Evidence for inspect_analysis_view; it does not reduce analysis. With summary detail, view {kind:"javascript-routes",collection:"routes",offset:0,limit:64} selects static route patterns; static routes do not prove reachability or the complete route set. Integrity mismatches fail by default; record-and-continue retains untrusted observed bytes and partial coverage. analysis_timeout_ms is a per-source provider budget. A host-only timeout needs a longer client deadline, not that budget; do not repeat unchanged work or assume it stopped. If configuration cannot be edited, report the host setting (Codex: mcp_servers.<server>.tool_timeout_sec, seconds).

reaTools.name: reconcile_javascript_runtime
reaTools.description:
Reconcile verified static JavaScript application graphs with existing passive web/Electron CDP, passive V8 Inspector, or provider-owned active Electron Evidence. Active Electron captures contribute an explicitly partial target-only runtime record; they never invent renderer scripts, frames, workers, or execution claims. Exact captured-source digests take priority over caller-declared file/URL mappings; target, frame, script, and worker ambiguity remains explicit, and source-map authority stays separate.

Declared Evidence fields accept complete records or {"kind":"retained-evidence","evidence_id":"ev_..."}. For a complete source, use the summary's parent_evidence_id. Advertised in reduced form by the compact input schema profile; the server still validates complete canonical inputs.
